figurative_meaning_en: High-value banknote that becomes invalid if marked or written upon
example_sentences_in_bangla: এই চুক্তিটা নম্বরী নোটের মতো, একটু ভুল হলেই সব শেষ।
তার পরিকল্পনা নম্বরী নোটের মতো সূক্ষ্ম, কোনো দাগ পড়লে বাতিল।
example_sentences_in_english: This deal is like a numbered note; one mistake and it's all over.
His plan is as delicate as a high-value banknote; any mark renders it invalid.
history: Refers to traditional banking practices in Bengal where high-denomination notes were marked with numbers for identification, but any additional writing invalidated them.
note: The idiom highlights the fragility of valuable items in Bengali cultural context of currency handling.
